why: policy.js, settings.js and profiles.js are byte-identical COPIES of the BGOS agent-browser rule tier, so a daemon-placed agent is judged by exactly the rules the desktop Agent Browser uses AND remembers an owner's answer exactly the way the desktop stores it. A second copy of a permission policy is how two hosts quietly come to disagree about what is sensitive; the sha256 below is what makes the copy checkable instead of merely claimed.

policy.js.aheadOfSource: Plugin 0.86.2 reads activating keys in every chord position. The BGOS policy mirror and its pin must take these bytes; outside-checkout mirrors were not changed.

profiles.js.whyThisOneToo: It owns WHERE a remembered answer is stored (agentGrants per agent key, the legacy alwaysGrants overlay, withAlwaysGrant, withTrustGrant, withoutTrustGrant). Without it the daemon host would have had to re-implement that shape, and 'Always allow' meaning two different things on two machines is the same class of drift the policy copy exists to prevent.

snapshot-target.js.whyThisOneToo: What names a gate's target from the host's own last snapshot, not from the agent's words. A machine and a desktop must read a target the same way.

whyADirectory: settings.js and profiles.js both do require("./policy"), so the copies keep their ORIGINAL filenames and sit together. package.json here pins type=commonjs, because the plugin root declares type=module and these files are CommonJS.
howToUpdate: Re-copy every file named above from its BGOS path, rerun the hashes, update this file, and run: HOAI_BROWSER_HOST_CORE_SOURCE=<BGOS agent-browser dir> npx tsx --test test/browser-host-core.vendor.test.ts
theHalfThisCannotSee: Nothing here fires when the BGOS originals change and these copies do not. That check lives on the BGOS side in frontend/electron-app/agent-browser/__tests__/hostCoreVendorPin.test.js, which pins the same hashes.
